subject.title: feat(ledger): add immutable action history core

question: Should ClawSweeper adopt this v1 immutable action-ledger schema and storage/replay contract as the foundation for workflow instrumentation?
rationale: The patch establishes a long-lived data, privacy, and security boundary; code review and tests cannot determine whether maintainers want this permanent architecture and compatibility commitment.

options.title: Accept the v1 contract
options.body: Approve the schema, identity, privacy, path, replay, and projection boundaries, with integrated workflow replay proof required before the stack lands.

options.title: Narrow the commitment
options.body: Require an explicit experimental boundary or smaller initial contract before downstream workflows become permanent writers and readers.

options.title: Pause the ledger direction
options.body: Hold the core and dependent instrumentation until maintainers select a different action-history architecture.

recommendation.title: Accept the v1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve the schema, identity, privacy, path, replay, and projection boundaries, with integrated workflow replay proof required before the stack lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the repository's core workflow, state, identity, and CrabFleet architecture, where Peter has the strongest historical ownership signal.
